parts.name: macaque
sources: MakeHuman (CC0): the low-poly body male1591, the skeleton game_engine and its weights, and the low-poly eyes (https://github.com/makehumancommunity/mpfb2); the tail is of World. CC0 1.0 (public domain): https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

A long-tailed macaque (khỉ đuôi dài, Macaca fascicularis): a male about 50 cm long without the tail, a tail longer than the body, a gray-brown coat with a lighter belly, a bare pink-brown face, dark hands and feet. It walks on four limbs.

Macaca fascicularis: 38 to 55 cm long without the tail, a tail of 40 to 65 cm; a male 5 to 9 kg, a female 3 to 4 kg; the coat gray-brown to red-brown, the belly lighter (Wikipedia, Crab-eating macaque).
The arms are about 0.9 of the legs (the intermembral index of macaques): a guess from the index, not a measurement of this shape.
Primates walk on four limbs in the order hind left, front right, hind right, front left (diagonal sequence). The time of a step and the stride are a guess.
